title: Bette Midler's 'Empty Bed Blues'
summary: Johnson accepts Midler's version because every artist should do it their own way.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I asked J. C., what do you think of Bette Midler's recording of your "Empty Bed Blues"? And he said, "It's all right. She's doing it her way. That's the way it's got to be." I thought this was interesting because, of course, Bessie Smith sang that and it made her famous and made him famous. He went on, "An artist has to do it the way they feel it. Would you expect Bessie Smith to do it like Bette Midler? No. As long as artists do it sincerely and in their way. This is their day, now. Then someone else will come along and do it their way. That keeps it going. You want the natural sequence of how they feel. They're not imitating anyone."
And I thought to myself, here is a man so flexible, so open, so unrelated to preconceived ideas, so content not to return to the way it was because he's so well understood
that you can never go back.
